gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly identifies the global basis problem's use of test functions restricted to K_i while the bilinear form integrates over all of Omega, and its repair explicitly corrects the global test space. This is the same mismatch that leaves the outside-of-K_i function unconstrained or the test argument inadmissible and prevents the claimed global orthogonality.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The declared global basis construction uses a local/restricted test space for a variational equation whose bilinear form is global, so it does not impose the equation against every admissible global test function and cannot establish the stated global kernel characterization.

component_coverage.gold_component: The global construction tests a globally integrated bilinear form only against w in V(K_i), leaving the function outside K_i unconstrained or making the global test argument inadmissible, so global orthogonality/kernel membership is not established.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that (msbasis) uses w in V(K_i) while B integrates over all of Omega, calls the problem ill-defined, and specifically repairs it by stating the global test space correctly.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 concerns an undefined projection in the coercivity lemma and the resulting ill-defined norm expression. It does not identify the separate missing C1/epsilon_0 multiplicative factor in the global energy estimate or the invalid coefficient-one claim.

ISSUE-006 diagnoses an invalid use of a discrete inf-sup condition as same-vector ellipticity in the Cea proof. It does not recognize that the declared V_ms is built on ordinary patches while the Cea proof analyzes the distinct symmetric-patch image space, nor the missing equality or transfer map between those spaces.

ISSUE-005 concerns the separate H-dependence of the Cea comparison parameter eta and the resulting positivity of beta_cem. It does not diagnose the incorrect inference that the resolution condition makes the independently defined stability constant C1 proportional to k^{-1}, or the resulting missing wavenumber scaling.

ISSUE-004 challenges the decay proof because nonlocalized k^2 contributions produce an N-factor and because a resolution hypothesis is omitted. It does not identify the distinct logarithmic loss caused by the stated threshold m approximately 4|log H|/|log theta|, nor the need to strengthen that oversampling threshold to recover uniform O(H) order.
